item.title: [Due in 1 day] SharePoint mobile apps for iOS and Android stop reaching SharePoint Server on 27 November 2026 and support SharePoint Online only
item.description:
Users who lose app access to on-premises SharePoint tend to fall back to the mobile browser or unmanaged apps, which may sit outside the app-protection policies that covered the SharePoint app.

SharePoint · deadline 2026-11-27 · Notify users who reach SharePoint Server from the mobile apps, update support documentation, and check that the browser path is covered by the same access and app-protection policies.

item.description:

item.title: [New] OneDrive fixes license evaluation that gave some plan combinations a 1 TB quota; users over the corrected quota go read-only from January 2027
item.description:
A read-only OneDrive stops sync and saves for affected users, which surfaces as helpdesk tickets and possible data held only on endpoints.

SharePoint · Run the over-quota report Microsoft links, re-license or clean up affected users before 29 Jan 2027, and brief the helpdesk.

item.title: [Message Center] MC1567262 Microsoft 365 Backup: Up to 10-year recovery windows for SharePoint and OneDrive
item.description:
Microsoft 365 Backup now allows configurable recovery windows up to 10 years for SharePoint and OneDrive, extending from the previous 2 years. Administrators can set recovery periods from 3 months to 10 years, while Exchange backup windows remain unchanged. No action is needed unless longer retention is desired.

Microsoft 365 suite, SharePoint Online, Microsoft OneDrive · stayInformed

item.title: [Message Center] MC1567261 OneDrive for Business: Bug fixes to ensure proper storage quota aligns with license limits
item.description:
OneDrive for Business will fix a bug causing incorrect 1 TB storage quotas for users with certain license combinations. Starting January 2027, quotas will match the actual storage plan, potentially reducing some users' quotas. Organizations should review usage, adjust licenses, and prepare for possible read-only states.

item.title: [New] SharePoint Online blocks new classic publishing sites and publishing features from 1 March 2027; new tenants also lose classic pages and custom scripts
item.description:
Custom scripting and classic pages are a long-standing persistence and phishing surface in SharePoint; Microsoft closing them is a hardening win, but provisioning automation that still creates publishing sites will fail.

SharePoint · Before 28 February 2027 find provisioning scripts and migrations that create classic publishing sites or activate publishing features, move them to modern sites, and inventory classic pages with the Microsoft 365 Assessment Tool.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Message Center] MC1565964 Microsoft SharePoint Online: Classic publishing restrictions begin March 1, 2027
item.description:
Starting March 1, 2027, SharePoint Online will block creation and activation of classic publishing sites and features, enforcing restrictions on custom scripting. New tenants face additional limits on classic pages. Administrators must update workflows and modernize pages before the rollout completes by October 2028.
